items.claim: The row's part-scoped vocative digit misreports the very inventory it cites: the range holds five bni_address verses, not four.
items.auditor_grounds: prov_device_inventory.json bni_address declares count_object 'verses containing the word-bound VOCATIVE token beni (my son; chirik), any position, pointed tier (E-1 corrected)', count 22, by_chapter 3:3 and 4:2; its refs inside Prov.3.1-Prov.4.27 are Prov.3.1, Prov.3.11, Prov.3.21, Prov.4.10 and Prov.4.20 - FIVE. The omitted verse is Prov.3.11, where the vocative stands as word 3, מוּסַ֣ר יְ֭הוָה בְּנִ֣י (oshb:Prov.3.11, words 1-3, byte tier); it drops out only under a verse-initial-opening count object, which the row never names while citing an any-position inventory. Not load-bearing for the seam: word 1 of oshb:Prov.3.1 is בְּ֭נִי at byte tier and the row closes on the PE at Prov.3.4 (pmarks, PE, tier-3 weak, single-witness), both independently verified, and the divine-name contrast the row draws is byte-true (no word-bound YHWH token anywhere in Prov.3.1-Prov.3.4; five across Prov.3.5-Prov.3.12).

items.adjudicator_grounds: CONFIRM at medium. Re-derived from bytes both ways. The inventory the row names (prov_device_inventory.json bni_address) declares its count object as verses containing the word-bound vocative token, any position, pointed tier, count 22, by_chapter 3:3 and 4:2; its refs inside Prov.3.1-Prov.4.27 are Prov.3.1, Prov.3.11, Prov.3.21, Prov.4.10 and Prov.4.20 - five - so the row's 'first of four bni_address occurrences within the part' and 'four heading this part' misreport the very object they cite. Independent sweep over verse_map_oshb.json (word-bound skeleton token בני, classified by the vowel under the nun at pointed tier): 22 vocative verses / 22 tokens, one per verse, in two attested spellings, בְּ֭נִי (oshb:Prov.3.1, word 1) and בְנִ֣י (oshb:Prov.5.20, word 3), plus 8 tsere-construct verses / 8 tokens, matching the inventory exactly; the row's '22 tokens book-wide' therefore coincides numerically only because every vocative verse carries one token - the inventory's unit is verses. The omitted verse stands at word 3 of oshb:Prov.3.11, מוּסַ֣ר יְ֭הוָה בְּנִ֣י (byte tier), which the row's 'recurring at 3.21, 4.10, and 4.20' skips; the row's list would be right only under an unnamed opening-position object (word 1 at Prov.3.1, Prov.3.21 and Prov.4.20; word 2 at Prov.4.10, שְׁמַ֣ע בְּ֭נִי, byte tier), while it cites the any-position inventory. items.claim: The rival narrower cut is rejected first on the ABSENCE of a parashah/disclosure object, an inference the book's mark law forbids.
items.auditor_grounds: The strongest_rejected_alternative reads that a cut after 3.24 'lacks any parashah or disclosure-object support, and both halves keep the same second-person, self-directed object, so the wider bound is kept instead'. The absence is byte-true - pmarks_Prov.json carries PE at Prov.3.18 and PE at Prov.3.35 with nothing between, and neither paseq nor K/Q anywhere in Prov.3.21-Prov.3.26 - but pmarks_Prov.json marks_note states in terms 'Absence is NEVER counterevidence', and the book strategy repeats it for the Writings parashah layer, so the first of the two grounds offered against the rival is inadmissible. It is not alone load-bearing: the second ground (both halves keep the same second-person, self-directed object) is positive and textual and stands on its own, and the row's own edges are untouched - the vocative בְּ֭נִי at oshb:Prov.3.21 (word 1, byte tier) and the object shift at Prov.3.27. Note the contrast within the same row: the in-span statement 'No petuchah or other disclosure-object note falls inside this span' is proper disclosure and is byte-true; only its conversion into a reason against the rival is the defect.
items.proposed_change: Field repair: rest the rival's rejection on the positive ground alone (the shared second-person, self-directed object across 3.21-3.24 and 3.25-3.26) and delete the 'lacks any parashah or disclosure-object support' clause; keep the in-span absence statement where it stands, as disclosure.
items.adjudicator_grounds: CONFIRM at medium. Re-derived from bytes: pmarks_Prov.json (WLC, single witness) marks PE at Prov.3.18 and PE at Prov.3.35 with no parashah entry between them, no paseq entry in Prov.3.21-Prov.3.26 (the chapter's one paseq is at Prov.3.28) and no K/Q entry there (chapter K/Q at Prov.3.15, Prov.3.27, Prov.3.28, Prov.3.30, Prov.3.34), so the row's absence statement is byte-true - and the strategy's parashah rule (tier-3 weak; absence never counterevidence), repeated in the inventory's own marks_note, bars converting it into a ground against the rival, which the rejected_alternative does as its first-listed reason ('lacks any parashah or disclosure-object support'). The inadmissible ground is also non-discriminating: the row's own close after Prov.3.26 has no parashah support either (the same PE pair at Prov.3.18 and Prov.3.35 brackets both cuts), so the absence argument would count equally against the shipped bound. Not load-bearing, hence medium: the second ground is positive and byte-true - the second-person self-directed object runs through both halves of the rival's cut, אִם תִּשְׁכַּ֥ב לֹֽא תִפְחָ֑ד and וְ֝שָׁכַבְתָּ֗ וְֽעָרְבָ֥ה שְׁנָתֶֽךָ at oshb:Prov.3.24, אַל תִּ֭ירָא at oshb:Prov.3.25, בְכִסְלֶ֑ךָ and רַגְלְךָ֣ at oshb:Prov.3.26 (all byte tier) - and the row's own edges stand: word 1 of oshb:Prov.3.21 is בְּ֭נִי (byte tier) and oshb:Prov.3.27 opens אַל תִּמְנַע ט֥וֹב מִבְּעָלָ֑יו (byte tier), shifting the object to a third party. Both sides of every seam weighed: front seam Prov.3.20|Prov.3.21 - the wisdom poem closes on the third-person cosmic couplet בְּ֭דַעְתּוֹ תְּהוֹמ֣וֹת נִבְקָ֑עוּ (oshb:Prov.3.20, byte tier) and the row opens on the vocative, so the C1 vocative rule decides (exact skeleton-token overlap 0); rear seam Prov.3.26|Prov.3.27 - the row closes on כִּֽי יְ֭הוָה יִהְיֶ֣ה בְכִסְלֶ֑ךָ (oshb:Prov.3.26, byte tier) with the addressee's own confidence as object, and the following unit opens the prohibition series with a third-party object, so the addressee-object shift decides (overlap 0), coherently with the following row, which argues the same seam from the same shift; the rival's interior cut Prov.3.24|Prov.3.25 - the sleep couplet closes on וְ֝שָׁכַבְתָּ֗ וְֽעָרְבָ֥ה שְׁנָתֶֽךָ and the fear couplet opens אַל תִּ֭ירָא מִפַּ֣חַד פִּתְאֹ֑ם (oshb:Prov.3.25, byte tier), and a root-level catchword straddles that cut, תִפְחָ֑ד (oshb:Prov.3.24, word 4) against מִפַּ֣חַד (oshb:Prov.3.25, word 3), byte tier, one root in two distinct tokens (exact-token overlap 0), which under the cross-seam cohesion rule argues continuity across the rival's cut - positive byte evidence the row could have used in place of the absence. Repair validated as proposed: rest the rival's rejection on the shared second-person self-directed object alone and keep the in-span absence sentence as disclosure; the straddling root may be added only as root-level (not exact-token) support. The register defect on 'the part's second lecture-opening slot' is real and stays at low.

current_row.boundary_rationale: שִׁמְע֣וּ בָ֭נִים (oshb:Prov.4.1) ('listen, sons') opens chapter 4 with a plural address, distinct from the singular address term shared by 3 of 4 lecture-openers in this part (3.1, 3.21, 4.10, 4.20). The row sets up a father's instruction (4.1-4.2), then recounts his own childhood as an only son (4.3) before introducing his own father's reported words with וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לִ֗י (oshb:Prov.4.4) ('and he said to me') in 4.4, a speech-frame device that itself completes one admonition-plus-consequence couplet. The row ends there, before the quoted instruction's own imperative pair opens fresh at 4.5.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping 4.1-4.9 as one unit was considered: nothing marks 4.4/4.5 with a parashah or disclosure object, so the seam rests on the speech-frame device alone (וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לִ֗י (oshb:Prov.4.4)) rather than corroborated tier-1-plus-tier-3 evidence, which is why this boundary is held at lower confidence rather than folded together.

Read the other way, as four openers out of a set that also contains this row's own plural opener at Prov.4.1, it would be 4 of 5; on neither reading is the shipped digit right, and the row never names the count object that would decide it (verse-initial opener vs the inventory's any-position vocative verse, of which Prov.3.1-Prov.4.27 holds five, Prov.3.11 included). The seam does not depend on the digit: the contrast the row actually needs is the plural שִׁמְע֣וּ בָ֭נִים (oshb:Prov.4.1, words 1-2, byte tier) against those singular openers, and that is byte-true whatever the tally.

Re-derived from bytes: all four verses the row lists carry the singular vocative at pointed tier - word 1 of oshb:Prov.3.1 בְּ֭נִי, word 1 of oshb:Prov.3.21 בְּ֭נִי, words 1-2 of oshb:Prov.4.10 שְׁמַ֣ע בְּ֭נִי, word 1 of oshb:Prov.4.20 בְּ֭נִי (all byte tier) - so 'the singular address term shared by 3 of 4 lecture-openers in this part (3.1, 3.21, 4.10, 4.20)' contradicts its own enumeration: 4 of 4. The only object under which a 3-of-4 digit is true is verse-initial position (word 1 at Prov.3.1, Prov.3.21 and Prov.4.20; word 2 at Prov.4.10), an object the row never names and which its wording ('address term shared by') does not describe; against the inventory's any-position object (prov_device_inventory.json bni_address, count 22, by_chapter 3:3 and 4:2) the range Prov.3.1-Prov.4.27 holds five vocative verses, Prov.3.11 included at word 3 (מוּסַ֣ר יְ֭הוָה בְּנִ֣י, oshb:Prov.3.11, byte tier). A false digit, not alone load-bearing, hence medium: the seam's actual warrant is the plural address שִׁמְע֣וּ בָ֭נִים (oshb:Prov.4.1, words 1-2, byte tier) against those singular openers, byte-true whatever the tally. Both sides of both seams weighed: front seam Prov.3.35|Prov.4.1 - the preceding unit closes on the third-person antithetic line כָּ֭בוֹד חֲכָמִ֣ים יִנְחָ֑לוּ (oshb:Prov.3.35, byte tier) under the PE at Prov.3.35 (pmarks_Prov.json, tier-3 weak, single witness), and the row opens on the plural vocative, so the C1 vocative rule decides with parashah corroboration (exact skeleton-token overlap 0), coherently with the preceding row, which closes itself at that mark; rear seam Prov.4.4|Prov.4.5 - the row's last verse carries the speech frame וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לִ֗י (oshb:Prov.4.4, words 2-3, byte tier) and the first quoted line יִֽתְמָךְ דְּבָרַ֥י לִבֶּ֑ךָ שְׁמֹ֖ר מִצְוֺתַ֣י וֶֽחְיֵֽה (words 4-9, byte tier), and the next unit opens קְנֵ֣ה חָ֭כְמָה קְנֵ֣ה בִינָ֑ה (oshb:Prov.4.5, byte tier), an imperative pair inside the same quoted speech, with no vocative, no parashah entry, no paseq and no K/Q anywhere in Prov.4.1-Prov.4.4 (nearest K/Q at Prov.4.16, next PE at Prov.4.19) and overlap 0, so that seam rests on the speech-frame device alone - which the row discloses, and the following row records that it inherits the frame from Prov.4.4; medium_low with the frontier flag is therefore calibrated and the lowband disposition (not a defect) stands. The register arm ('in this part', 'this part's rows') is real, low. Repair validated with one correction: the proposed '4 of 4 verse-initial openers' is itself wrong for Prov.4.10 (word 2); restate as opening-position vocative (word 1 or 2), 4 of 4 across the listed verses, or as the inventory's any-position verse count, 5 across Prov.3-4.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The span opens with a nominal characterization, "אָדָ֣ם בְּ֭לִיַּעַל אִ֣ישׁ אָ֑וֶן" (oshb:Prov.6.12; “A worthless person, a man of iniquity”, web:Prov.6.12), and continues as a chain of participial clauses sharing that one grammatical subject: a perverse mouth (6.12), winking eyes / signaling feet / motioning fingers (6.13), and a scheming heart (6.14) — a cumulative character portrait rather than direct address or imperative instruction. The chain closes when "עַל כֵּ֗ן" (oshb:Prov.6.15; “therefore”, web:Prov.6.15) draws the causal consequence (sudden, remedyless calamity) from the accumulated portrait, tying 6:15 back to the subject introduced in 6:12 and closing the unit before the numerical formula of 6:16 opens a new list-governed unit.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 6:12-15 as an admonition_unit was rejected because its verbs are third-person participles describing a character type rather than second-person imperatives addressed to the reader; the cohesion is a shared grammatical subject carried across four verses, not a single couplet, so single_proverb was also rejected.
observed_substrate_signals: oshb:Prov.6.12 nominal-subject opener "אָדָ֣ם בְּ֭לִיַּעַל אִ֣ישׁ אָ֑וֶן"
oshb:Prov.6.13 three-part participial body-part chain (eyes/feet/fingers)
oshb:Prov.6.14 heart-clause + discord-sowing clause, ketiv/qere pair
oshb:Prov.6.15 causal "עַל כֵּ֗ן" drawing the consequence
current_row.device_notes: Synthetic, cumulative parallelism (portrait building toward one consequence), not antithetic. A petuchah closes oshb:Prov.6.15 in WLC (tier-3, single-witness), consistent with the boundary argued from the causal clause. A petuchah is also attested one verse earlier, at oshb:Prov.6.11 (tier-3 corroboration, single witness), closing the sluggard unit that precedes this span; it is disclosed here as the adjoining mark rather than as evidence for the 6:12 opening argued above. A ketiv/qere note attaches to 6:14 (oshb:Prov.6.14: ketiv "מדנים", plural spelling, against qere "מִדְיָנִ֥ים") — disclosed here because the span touches it; the note affects the spelling of "discord," not the boundary. A paseq seg is also attested at 6:14; the inventory marks presence, not position, so no intra-verse placement is claimed here either. This proverb_cluster stands outside C1's instruction_lecture/wisdom_poem default; the third-person participial portrait argued above, not an imperative address, is the byte-grounded deviation.

items.claim: The span's bytes are one syntactically continuous sentence rather than atomic sayings cohering, so proverb_cluster mis-types the unit the row itself describes.
items.auditor_grounds: Byte tier, every run spliced from the staged verse map: 6:12 carries the run's only nominal subject, אָדָ֣ם בְּ֭לִיַּעַל אִ֣ישׁ אָ֑וֶן , and its first participial predicate, ה֝וֹלֵ֗ךְ עִקְּשׁ֥וּת פֶּֽה ; 6:13 is entirely dependent - קֹרֵ֣ץ בְּ֭עֵינָו מֹלֵ֣ל בְּרַגְלָ֑ו מֹ֝רֶ֗ה בְּאֶצְבְּעֹתָֽיו - three participial forms with prepositional phrases, carrying no subject noun and no prefix- or suffix-conjugation verb of its own, and 6:14 continues under the same third-person masculine singular reference, תַּֽהְפֻּכ֨וֹת בְּלִבּ֗וֹ , before the apodosis opens at 6:15 with עַל כֵּ֗ן . The staged extract carries no morphology layer, so the form reading is argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings: WEB renders 6:13 as bare relative clauses depending on 6:12, “who winks with his eyes, who signals with his feet, who motions with his fingers,” (web:Prov.6.13). A proverb_cluster row claims that atomic sayings cohere as one unit; these member verses are not separable sayings, since 6:13 cannot stand as a saying at all, and the row's own rationale describes the span as one cumulative portrait resolved by a causal clause. The collection's ruled precedent types a syntactically continuous single sentence spanning verses as one proverb-unit regardless of verse count, which is the byte situation here. The span itself is not in question: the causal opener at 6:15 ties the apodosis back to 6:12, a petuchah closes oshb:Prov.6.15 in WLC (tier-3, single-witness, inventory-confirmed), and 6:16 opens the numerical formula.
